from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [

            "GPS history tracks distance: the integral.",
            "Two faces of motion, linked by time."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Speedometer and the GPS", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        speedometer = Circle(radius=1.0, color=WHITE)
        needle = Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.8, color=WHITE)
        
        gps_path = VMobject(color=RED)
        gps_path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid['C3'], self.grid['D4'], self.grid['E5'], self.grid['F6']])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(speedometer, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(needle, 'B2')
        self.play(FadeIn(speedometer), FadeIn(needle), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Rotate(needle, angle=-PI/2, about_point=self.grid['B2'], rate_func=there_and_back))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(gps_path), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.play(FadeIn(glow), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(glow.animate.move_to(self.grid['F6']))
        self.play(FadeOut(glow))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Accumulating rate returns the original function.",
            "Volume growth is the rate of flow.",
            "The area function's rate is the curve.",
            "Fundamental Theorem links accumulation and change.",
            "Integration undoes differentiation's work."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part I)", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x + 0.5, color="#FFFFFF")
        curve_label = MathTex("f(t)", color="#FFFFFF").scale(0.7)
        
        area_func = Polygon(*[axes.c2p(0, 0), *[axes.c2p(x, 0.5 * x + 0.5) for x in np.linspace(0, 2, 20)], axes.c2p(2, 0)], color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.4)
        area_label = MathTex("A(x)", color="#00FFFF").scale(0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(curve, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(curve_label, 'A3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), Write(curve_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(area_func, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, 'C4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(area_func), Write(area_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFCC00")
        derivative_label = MathTex("A'(x) = f(x)", color="#FFCC00").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(derivative_label, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(derivative_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#AA00FF")
        ftc_text = Text("FTC", color="#AA00FF", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(ftc_text, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(ftc_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        line = Line(start=axes.c2p(0, 0), end=axes.c2p(0, 2), color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(line, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Create(line))
        self.play(line.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Inverse Operation: Differentiation and Integration", 
                          ["Differentiation and integration are inverse operations.", 
                           "Balloon volume tracks its expansion rate.", 
                           "Antiderivatives reverse the growth process."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a function and its derivative side-by-side
        F_x = MathTex("F(x)", color="#FFFFFF")
        f_x = MathTex("f(x) = F'(x)", color="#FFFFFF")
        arrow = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(F_x, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(f_x, "B4")
        
        self.play(Write(F_x), GrowArrow(arrow), Write(f_x))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize reverse flow from integral to function
        reverse_arrow = Arrow(start=RIGHT, end=LEFT, color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(reverse_arrow, "C3")
        
        int_symbol = MathTex(r"\int f(x) dx", color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(int_symbol, "C2")
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(reverse_arrow), Write(int_symbol))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Demonstrate canceling operations with inverse processes
        formula = MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx} \int f(x) dx = f(x)", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(formula, "E2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Speedometer and the GPS
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Rate of Change' vs. 'Accumulation'. Use a visual of a car: The speedometer shows instantaneous speed (derivative), while the GPS tracking history shows total distance traveled (integral).
sections.example: A cat running: Its current speed at any moment is the derivative of its position; the total ground covered over time is the integral of that speed curve.

sections.title: The Geometric Connection
sections.content: Establish the prerequisite: The slope of a tangent line (derivative) vs. the area under a curve (integral). Visualize a bar chart evolving into a smooth curve, showing that as the width of rectangles approaches zero, the sum becomes an integral.
sections.example: Visualizing the area under a velocity-time graph as the total displacement of a robot arm.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part I)
sections.content: Define the relationship: If you accumulate the rate of change of a function, you return to the original function. Provide the formal visualization: The area function A(x) changes at a rate equal to the height of the curve f(x).
sections.example: The 'Water Tank' analogy: The rate at which water flows into a tank (f(x)) is the derivative of the total volume of water in the tank (A(x)).

sections.title: The Inverse Operation: Differentiation and Integration
sections.content: Explain that integration and differentiation are inverse processes, similar to multiplication and division. Show a flowchart: F(x) --(diff)--> f(x) --(int)--> F(x) + C.
sections.example: A balloon being inflated: The rate of change of the radius (derivative) determines the growth of the volume, and integrating that growth rate recovers the volume function.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting the power of this relationship: It allows us to calculate areas of complex, irregular shapes using simple algebraic formulas (antiderivatives).
sections.example: Calculating the precise surface area of a uniquely shaped dragon wing by integrating the curvature function derived from its profile.
